Every morning, before the rest of the lab arrived, Tomas checked on the organoids. They sat in their incubator like a row of small pearls, each one a few millimeters across, floating in pink medium. Under the microscope he could see the folds starting to form, and the clusters of cells arranging themselves into layers. It was strange to think that these tiny balls were following the same schedule that a developing brain follows. Weeks passed; the structures grew more complex. One morning he noticed faint waves of electrical activity sweeping across the surface of the oldest organoid, rhythmic and slow, like a heartbeat. He stood very still for a long time, afraid that if he moved he would break the spell.
